text: OSPF is a link-state IGP. Routers exchange link-state information, build an LSDB for an area, and run SPF to calculate routes. Area 0 is the backbone for inter-area connectivity.

BGP is a path-vector routing protocol. A BGP speaker exchanges reachability plus path attributes and applies policy to select and advertise routes. eBGP operates between autonomous systems; iBGP distributes BGP routes inside an AS.
EVPN uses BGP to distribute Layer 2 and Layer 3 reachability. A Type 2 route advertises MAC and optionally IP information. EVPN can provide a control plane for VXLAN fabrics.
VXLAN carries overlay segments across an IP underlay using UDP encapsulation. A 24-bit VNI identifies an overlay segment and offers a much larger segmentation space than VLAN IDs.

MTU problems often appear when small packets work but larger packets fail. Tunnels add overhead, reducing the payload that fits without fragmentation. Path MTU Discovery also depends on appropriate control messages reaching endpoints.
Spanning Tree creates a loop-free active Layer 2 topology. A blocked redundant link is often intentional protection against switching loops rather than evidence that STP is broken.
When direct IP reachability works but hostname resolution fails, investigate resolver configuration, reachability to the DNS server, policy for DNS traffic, and the resolver's upstream behavior.
Safe network automation limits blast radius with prechecks, configuration diff, staged rollout, explicit failure thresholds, rollback, post-change validation, and audit logging.
